sentence: This project studies how condensate formation drives tumor initiation and gene expression in ependymoma driven by a fusion oncoprotein, and how drugs change condensates.
This project builds an open-source toolkit for markerless motion capture that produces datasets and metadata that can be easily shared.
This project studies how tumors change their physical microenvironment and host cells, and how these changes shape disease progression and treatment.
This project builds computational tools that use machine learning to model how RNA folds.
This project studies how DNA methylation and microRNAs control the development of neural crest and mesoderm cells from human embryonic stem cells.
This project tries to develop a strategy that delivers drugs to the kidney by using solute carrier transporters.
This project builds and tests a fluorescence molecular imaging agent that helps show sessile serrated adenomas, a pre-cancerous lesion of the colon.
This project studies how rhesus macaques infected with simian-human immunodeficiency virus make broadly neutralizing antibodies against HIV-1 to guide vaccine design.
This project builds marmoset models of Alzheimer's disease to study the cellular and molecular root causes of the disease.
This project builds a chip of vascularized human tissue that models antibody-mediated rejection of allografts and monitors their injury with a biosensor.
This project builds a drug delivery technology that improves the use of previously discarded organs and outcomes after organ transplantation.
This project tests whether podocytes signal the proximal tubule to protect it from injury and slow diabetic kidney disease.
This project studies redox biology, the chemistry of oxidation and reduction in biological systems that shapes metabolism and signaling.
This project develops an injectable hydrogel that restores salivary gland function by reactivating stem cells to regenerate saliva-producing cells.
This project brings together basic, translational and population science to improve outcomes for patients with cancer.
This project studies how the brain adapts after nerve damage or limb loss, looking at cell, synapse and structure changes that affect recovery.
This project combines large-scale DNA synthesis and single-cell sequencing to study how genes that pattern the developing nervous system are regulated.
This project studies how a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease disrupts microglia, brain circuits and synapse remodeling in rodent models.
This project tries to find the substances in human breast milk that trigger cancer cell death.
This project tests whether central auditory tests can assess or predict effects of HIV infection on the central nervous system in children.
